finding_verdicts.reason: The evaluation expects inferred facts to be marked unconfirmed. This is an editorial accuracy requirement, not a configuration-library import or environment read.
The JSON fixture asks for preparation to record an onboarding flow and sets should_trigger to true. It contains no capture implementation or upload instruction.
The phrase 'at 1:40' identifies a viewer-retention timestamp in a test query. It does not invoke the at scheduler.
The evaluation prohibits inventing figures, customers, personas, or calls to action. It specifies content accuracy and performs no system inspection.
The expected output diagnoses video addressability through titled segments and starting states. These are script structure requirements, not host reconnaissance.
The fixture limits a script review to how an author's performance claim is expressed. No system information is requested or collected.
The evaluation requires customer names, tenant IDs, internal hostnames, and pricing to stay off screen. This prevents disclosure rather than collecting system identifiers.
The paragraph quotes production advice about small takes, editing mistakes, and synchronized narration. It contains no system discovery instructions.
The bullet requires checking music licenses for commercial use and derivatives. This is asset licensing guidance, not system reconnaissance.
Internal hostnames appear in the Off-limits list of information that must not be recorded. There is no hostname discovery or collection.
The paragraph explains that enterprise recordings can be forwarded and reviewed later. It justifies disclosure precautions and specifies no network probing.
The bracketed unconfirmed marker identifies a missing measurement in a draft script. No configuration library or environment variable is accessed.
The spoken agenda 'at 0:20' is a timeline entry in a negative video-script example. It is not an at scheduling command.
This is a table-of-contents link to the script-review output example. The heading describes reviewing narration, not inspecting a system.
The paragraph explains that chapter organization made a video addressable without shortening it. Addressability refers to finding video segments, not network addresses.

The heading introduces a Markdown example of reviewing a video script. It does not request host information or execute discovery commands.

content.user_title: Write Technical Video Scripts Ready for Recording
content.value_statement: Technical videos lose clarity when narration, screen actions, and timing are planned separately. This skill combines them into a script with recording states and cuts.
actual_capabilities: Turn supplied posts, documentation, changelogs, or demos into visual and narration beats.
Select video formats using audience needs, deadlines, production resources, and effort constraints.
Estimate runtime from measured speaking rate and per-beat pauses, builds, or loading time.
Prepare chapters, cut plans, starting states, and recording briefs with sensitive information exclusions.
Review existing scripts for missing logic, repetition, and lines that are difficult to speak.
Plan animated storyboards, short vertical clips, accessible narration, and caption correction workflows.
limitations: Does not record, edit, render, or publish videos or generate finished animation assets.
Runtime estimates require the recorder's measured speaking rate and realistic operation timings.
Does not guarantee retention improvements, factual accuracy of supplied claims, or accessibility compliance.
Caption translations need fluent review, and platform rules or commercial asset licenses need separate verification.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Technical Post
use_cases.description: Convert a published engineering post into a focused screencast with an opening result, narration beats, and a cut plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Enterprise Walkthrough
use_cases.description: Create a recording brief with seeded data, repeatable starting states, version disclosures, and an explicit list of sensitive information exclusions.

use_cases.title: Review a Tutorial Script
use_cases.description: Find confusing transitions, repeated explanations, and difficult narration while keeping original lines beside suggested replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Screencast Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me script a technical screencast about [topic] for [audience]. Ask one question at a time until the promise and source are clear.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: define the video before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Existing Source
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [source text] into a [runtime] walkthrough for [audience]. Provide visual actions, narration, starting states, chapters, a cut plan, and recording brief.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert approved source material into a recording plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review Retention Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [script] alongside [retention observations] for a [format] video. Map problems to beats, rank their impact, and show original lines beside suggested replacements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: diagnose an existing video without replacing the entire script.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Animated Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Storyboard [source claims] for [audience] within [runtime] and [production constraints]. Include animation actions, required assets, music cues, narration, timing, and cuttable beats.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a motion design handoff with limited production resources.

output_examples.input: Plan the opening for a four-minute webhook-signing tutorial using Node 20 and a free test account.
output: Visual: A test webhook is rejected, and the terminal displays the signature error.
Narration: This handler rejects a forged webhook. In four minutes, you will add signature verification using Node 20 and a free test account.
Starting state: Open the supplied demo with seeded data and a rejected-request result ready to reproduce.
Timing: Budget 25 seconds, including a silent pause to read the result.

output_examples.input: Review this screencast line: Change this to that, and now it works.
output: Issue: The narration does not name the field, value, or observable result.
Suggested replacement: Set the retry limit to three attempts. Run the test and read the reported attempt count.
Recording check: Confirm that the displayed result matches the narration before approving the beat.

best_practices: Supply approved source material, a specific audience, and one outcome before requesting a full script.
Measure speaking rate and rehearse each starting state before accepting the runtime budget.
Use seeded data, review captions, and verify claims and licenses before publication.
anti_patterns: Requesting a complete script without defining the viewer, outcome, or source material.
Estimating duration from narration alone while ignoring builds, loading, and reading pauses.
Recording real customer data or leaving narration dependent on unnamed screen positions.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a script with visual actions, narration, starting states, timing estimates, chapters where appropriate, a cut plan, and recording guidance.

faq.question: Can it create or edit the finished video?
faq.answer: No. It prepares scripts and storyboards for a person or production tool to record, animate, edit, and publish.

faq.question: Can it adapt existing documentation or blog posts?
faq.answer: Yes. It extracts supported claims from the source and reorganizes them into video beats rather than copying the original headings.

faq.question: How does it estimate runtime?
faq.answer: It divides narration word count by the recorder's measured speaking rate, then adds per-beat operation times and deliberate pauses.

faq.question: Can it review a script I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks logic, repetition, and speakability, ranks findings, and presents proposed changes beside the original lines.

faq.question: Does it support captions and synthetic voiceovers?
faq.answer: It provides caption correction, translation review, pronunciation, and voiceover planning guidance. Audio generation and caption publication require separate tools.
